definition: Multiple AI agents working in parallel or in collaboration to complete a task faster or more robustly than a single agent.
details: A swarm splits work across specialist or duplicate agents, then combines their results — polling several models for consensus, exploring many solution branches at once, or dividing a large job into sub-tasks. The pattern trades compute for coverage and resilience.
story: Think of a chess player who never commits to a move blindly — they consider the board, try an action, watch what changes, and only then decide what is next. In plain words: Multiple AI agents working in parallel or in collaboration to complete a task faster or more robustly than a single agent. Here is how it actually plays out: A swarm splits work across specialist or duplicate agents, then combines their results — polling several models for consensus, exploring many solution branches at once, or dividing a large job into sub-tasks. The model stops being a one-shot answer machine and becomes a coworker that checks its own work. That loop of reason, act, and observe is Agent Swarms.
